claims.text: Language models are highly sensitive to epistemic markers in prompts, with question-answering accuracy varying by more than 80%.
Expressions of high certainty in prompts result in a 7% decrease in language model accuracy compared to expressions of low certainty.
Factive verbs in prompts reduce language model question-answering performance.
Evidentials in prompts improve language model question-answering performance.
In a popular pretraining dataset, markers of uncertainty are associated with answers on question-answering websites.
In a popular pretraining dataset, markers of certainty are associated with questions on question-answering websites.
Language model sensitivity to epistemic markers may be driven by mimicking observed language associations in training data rather than reflecting true epistemic uncertainty.

methodologies.name: Epistemic marker prompt injection analysis
methodologies.description: A typology of epistemic markers was developed and 50 markers were injected into prompts for question answering to evaluate LM performance sensitivity and pretraining text co-occurrence patterns.
conditions: Injection of 50 epistemic markers into question-answering prompts
Co-occurrence analysis of markers in a pretraining dataset
